item.title: 95 million-year-old Spinosaurus had a scimitar-shaped head crest and waded through the Sahara's rivers like a 'hell heron'
item.description: Researchers have identified a new Spinosaurus species with a blade-like crest in Niger, changing our understanding of dinosaur evolution and behavior.

item.title: In a 'race against time,' archaeologists uncovered Roman-era footprints from a Scottish beach before the tide washed them away
item.description: Archaeologists raced against the tide to record a unique set of footprints made 2,000 years ago on a Scottish beach.

item.title: Bungled Boeing Starliner mission was the highest order of mishap that put stranded astronauts at risk, report says
item.description: The 2024 Starliner mission, which left astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams stranded in space for nine months, has received NASA's worst mishap classification in a damning report.

item.title: New tech allows parents to 'score' IVF embryos for desirable traits — and it's in desperate need of regulation
item.description: Companies now offer polygenic embryo selection to prospective parents undergoing IVF. But the technology is dangerously underregulated.

item.title: 'Proof by intimidation': AI is confidently solving 'impossible' math problems. But can it convince the world's top mathematicians?
item.description: AI could soon spew out hundreds of mathematical proofs that look "right" but contain hidden flaws, or proofs so complex we can't verify them. How will we know if they're right?

item.title: A coffin holding a dead 'princess' fell from an eroded cliff over 100 years ago — archaeologists just solved a major mystery about her
item.description: Dendrochronological analysis of a mysterious log coffin that tumbled from a cliff a century ago reveals clues to life in Roman-era Poland.

item.title: Artemis II update: NASA targets March 6 for launch of historic moon mission following successful 'wet dress rehearsal'
item.description: NASA is targeting March 6 as the earliest possible launch date for the Artemis II mission to the moon following a successful 'wet dress rehearsal' on Thursday.

item.title: Your own voice could be your biggest privacy threat. How can we stop AI technologies exploiting it?
item.description: Voices contain countless cues about their owners, and new research suggests that computers might use them to facilitate a range of bad behaviors.

item.title: 'Universal' nasal-spray vaccine protects against viruses, bacteria and allergens in mice
item.description: In an early animal test, a new nasal-spray vaccine has shown promise against a variety of germs and a common allergen, scientists report.

item.title: Ancient 'Asgard' microbe may have used oxygen long before it was plentiful on Earth, offering new clue to origins of complex life
item.description: A new study suggests that ancient microbes once cast as oxygen haters may have actually learned to use the gas, offering a clue to how the first complex cells — and, eventually, all plants and animals — evolved.
